transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I can’t seem to stop worrying once something gets in my head. It can be about my mother getting up at night, or a grant report, or whether I missed something at work. I make lists and try to redirect myself, but it just doesn’t really… get shelved.
Do these worries ever feel like intrusive, unwanted thoughts that keep popping into your mind even when you try not to think about them?
Yes… I think so. Once a worry starts, it just keeps coming back even when I’m trying not to think about it. I’ll make lists or try to focus on something else, but it doesn’t really stay put.
When these thoughts get stuck, do you feel driven to do something over and over to make the anxiety go down?

I don’t think so… not in a specific way. I might try to make a list or check my notes, but it’s not like I have to do something over and over exactly. It’s more just… trying to settle my mind, I guess.
Do you find yourself worrying about many different parts of your life, rather than mainly one specific problem?

Yes… it’s not just one thing anymore. Over the past year it’s sort of spread — my mother, money, work decisions, deadlines, the house. Even small things can start feeling like they’re going to unravel.
Do you feel like your worrying is hard to control?

Yes. That’s… honestly why I came in. Once I start worrying about something — my mother getting up at night, or a grant report, or whether I missed something at work — I can’t really put it away. I make lists, I try to redirect myself, but it just keeps sitting there in my mind.
Do you often feel restless or keyed up?
I’m not sure… maybe sometimes. I wouldn’t say I’m pacing around or anything. It’s more like I have trouble feeling settled, if that makes sense.
Have you been worrying like this for at least six months?
Yes… it’s been more than six months. I guess about a year or so — maybe a little over. It started after my mother moved in with me after her fall.
Has this worrying been interfering with your daily life?

Yes… it has. Mostly at work. I’ve started missing small but important details at the library, which isn’t really like me. And I had to hand off part of a grant presentation because I froze. I don’t like saying that, but… it’s made me question whether I’m handling leading my team the way I should.
Do you feel this started because of the stress of your mother moving in after her fall?
Yes… I think so. It’s been going on since she moved in after the fall — about a year and two months now.
If your mother had not moved in after her fall, do you think this level of worrying would still be happening?
I don’t really know. I mean… maybe not this much. It’s hard to separate it from everything that happened.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?
I… I don’t know. Not really depressed, I don’t think. I’ve been overwhelmed, but I wouldn’t call it feeling down exactly.
Do you find yourself worrying even about things that have nothing to do with your mother moving in?

Yes… it’s not just about my mother anymore. I worry about money, work things—staff decisions, deadlines—the house. Even small things can start to feel like they’re going to unravel. And then I wonder if I’m being a good enough daughter, too.
Have you been feeling more tired than usual?

Yes… more tired, I guess. I don’t sleep very well most nights. I lie there going over the day, thinking through what could go wrong. And if I hear my mother up during the night, then I’m awake for another hour or two. By the time I get to the library, I feel like I haven’t really rested.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yes… somewhat. At work, during cataloging reviews or meetings, I’ll be staring right at the screen or the agenda and then realize I haven’t really taken in any of it. My mind’s gone off to some problem I feel like I should’ve prevented.
Do you often feel muscle tension, like tightness in your shoulders, neck, or jaw?

Yes… mostly my neck and shoulders. By the end of the day they feel sort of locked up, like I’ve been bracing myself. And I do catch myself clenching my jaw sometimes, answering emails or listening for my mother in the next room.
Have you been feeling sad most days?
I don’t know… not most days, I don’t think. I get worn down, but I wouldn’t really call it sad exactly.
If your mother no longer needed your care, do you think you would still be worrying this much?

I think… probably, yes. It started with my mother, but over this past year it’s sort of spread. I worry about money, decisions at work, deadlines, the house… whether I’m doing enough as a daughter. Even small things can start to feel like they’re about to come apart.
Do you feel your worrying is more intense than the situation really calls for?

Yes… I think so. It feels bigger than it should. It started with my mother, but now I can get caught up worrying about money, work decisions, deadlines, the house… even small things feel like they might unravel.
Compared with the stress about your mother, does your worrying now feel mostly centered on that situation, or has it taken on a life of its own?

It’s… not just my mother anymore. That’s where it started, but now it feels like it’s spread into everything — money, work decisions, deadlines, the house. Even small things can start to feel like they’re going to unravel.
Do you feel your anxiety is mainly a reaction to your mother moving in after her fall?

Not mainly, no. It began with that, after her fall… but over the past year it’s gone beyond her safety. I worry about finances, decisions at work, deadlines, the house, whether I’m doing enough as a daughter. Even little things can start to feel like they’re about to unravel.
